result.summary: Independently re-verified REQ-023 (waitlist auto-promotion on a freed seat, halting at T-24h) at commit 3849290, branch feature/WF02-REQ-023. Did not trust TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 report, the test report, or requirement_status.yaml history as substitutes for my own re-derivation. 1. Read docs/agents/design/REQ-023.md in full against all 7 acceptance criteria (§9's AC-to-design-element map). Every AC maps to a concrete, non-deferred design element. Both design questions (§0 trigger point, §5 at-most-once notification) are resolved with a marker-free mechanism, not deferred. §8 names 4 open questions explicitly (QR delivery, T-24h visibility precision, send-failure UX, REQ-025's future ledger key) rather than silently resolving them -- none of the 7 ACs in scope depend on those open items. Confirmed 'no schema change' myself: git diff master...HEAD --stat -- apps/bot/drizzle produced zero output. 2. Read apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts's isAutoPromotionHalted (lines 734-746) and apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts's decidePromotionEligibility/promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible/withdrawRegistration in full, comparing line-by-line against the design: the FOR UPDATE lock discipline on `events` (identical to registerForEvent, REQ-020 §3.2), the (created_at, id) tie-break on the waitlist SELECT (identical to getWaitlistPosition, REQ-021), the single writeAuditLog call reached only on the 'promoted' branch, and the first-match-wins eligibility table exactly as specified (event-not-eligible -> halted-t24h -> capacity-full -> ok). Read apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.ts in full: the single sendPromotionNotification call site (lines 140-148) is gated on `outcome.kind === 'withdrawn' && outcome.promotion.kind === 'promoted'` -- this is AC7's structural single-notification argument, re-derived directly from the code, not copied from the design doc's own claim. The blocked-user guard (lines 197-199, S10 rework) skips the send only, after the promotion/audit/seat-accounting has already committed -- matches design §6.2 exactly. 3. Re-ran npm run lint myself: 0 errors, 2 pre-existing apps/web LCP warnings (Footer.tsx, Nav.tsx) -- unrelated to this diff, matches TEST-RUNNER's report. Re-ran npm run build myself: apps/web (Next.js/Turbopack) compiled successfully; apps/bot (tsc -p tsconfig.json) clean, zero errors. Re-ran npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism from the repo root myself, twice: once with no scratch Postgres reachable (17 files, 169 passed / 43 skipped = 212 total) confirming the DB-suite's self-skip guard fires correctly, then again after standing up my own scratch Postgres (docker-compose.yml, port 55432) and running `npx drizzle-kit migrate` myself (applied cleanly, zero new migration files) -- second run: 17 files / 212 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed. Matches TEST-RUNNER's reported 212-test count exactly. 4. Independent re-verification of the 4 items this task specifically called out, using my own fixtures against my own scratch Postgres (apps/bot/scratch-rv-req023.ts and scratch-rv-req023-race.ts, both deleted after the run, never reusing BACKEND-DEV's or TEST-RUNNER's scratch harnesses): - AC2 T-24h boundary, my own timestamps (2026-09-07T12:00:00.000Z base): isAutoPromotionHalted returned true at exactly T-24h, false at T-24h+1ms, true at T-24h-1ms, false at 48h out, true at 12h out -- exact match to the design's <= boundary rule, no off-by-one. - AC7 structural single-notification argument: read apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.ts myself (see §2 above) and confirmed the single gated call site directly in the code, not by trusting the design doc's or TEST-RUNNER's restatement of it. - AC8 blocked user, my own fixture: capacity=1 event, one admitted user, a blocked candidate registered before a non-blocked candidate (forcing the blocked candidate to rank first on the waitlist), single withdrawal freeing one seat. DB-level result: blocked candidate correctly promoted (admission='admitted', fresh qr_token written, exactly 1 registration.promote audit row), non-blocked candidate correctly left waitlisted (only one seat freed). This confirms the promotion/audit/seat-accounting side of AC8 independently of the handler-level send-skip already confirmed by code read in §2. - Atomic-capacity/promotion concurrency test, run fresh by me at 20 iterations (my own fixture: capacity=3 event, 3 admitted + 1 waitlisted seeded per iteration, one admitted user's withdrawal raced via Promise.all against a fresh registrant's registerForEvent for the same event): admitted count was exactly 3 on all 20/20 iterations, never 4, never <3. No over- or under-admission under fresh concurrent load. 5. Confirmed full requirement scope: git diff master...HEAD --stat shows exactly the files the design describes (domain/event.ts, domain/registration.ts + its db test file, domain/user.ts, handlers/withdraw.ts + its test file, i18n/{types,ru,en}.ts, docs/design, docs/test-specs, docs/issues/ISS-0020.yaml, plus this run's own handoffs/test-report) -- nothing stray. Grepped apps/bot/src for TODO/FIXME/XXX: zero matches. git status --porcelain clean (scratch files and scratch Postgres container/volume torn down after use). All design-doc-listed files present and match §1's reused-vs-new list exactly. 6. Judgment on ISS-0020 (REQ-018's staff.ts has the same S10 blocked-user gap REQ-023 just fixed, MAJOR, explicitly out of scope for this diff): this is a real, live security-invariant violation in already-merged, already-deployed production code (apps/bot/src/handlers/staff.ts) -- not a hypothetical or test-only gap. A blocked user assigned as EventStaff today would actually receive a Telegram message in production, violating security-invariants.md S10's 'blocked users are skipped in both cases' clause, right now, independent of whether REQ-023 merges. It is correctly out of scope for THIS diff (staff.ts is REQ-018's file, untouched by REQ-023's changes; fixing it here would violate scope discipline) and does not block this release -- REQ-023's own diff has no such gap (confirmed by fixture and code read above). However, given it is a live, exploitable violation of a named security invariant in production rather than a design/process nit, I recommend ORCH escalate its priority above the general MAJOR-issue backlog cadence -- e.g., queue it as the next WF-03 fix-run rather than letting it sit alongside lower-urgency filed issues, since every day it remains open is a day the S10 invariant is actively violated for real users, not just a latent risk. Overall: every independent check I ran -- lint, build, full test suite from the repo root (with and without DB), an independently-constructed AC2 boundary check with my own timestamps, an independent code read confirming AC7's structural argument, an independently-constructed AC8 blocked-user fixture, and a fresh 20-iteration concurrency race against the real Postgres -- agrees with all six prior gates (CODE-DESIGNER/VALIDATOR, BACKEND-DEV, REVIEWER, SECURITY-REVIEWER, TEST-DESIGNER/VALIDATOR, TEST-RUNNER). No half-implemented scope, no stray TODOs, clean git tree, all design-doc-listed files present. This is the second concurrency-critical function reusing REQ-020's lock discipline (after REQ-022's withdrawRegistration), and it holds under fresh concurrent load exactly as REQ-022's did.
